Rodney Strickland was born on July 11, 1966.
Rod Strickland is an American basketball coach and former professional basketball player.
Rod Strickland is currently the head coach at Long Island University.
Prior to LIU, Rod Strickland served as the program manager for the NBA G League's professional path.
Rod Strickland played college basketball at DePaul University.
Rod Strickland was awarded All-American honors during his college career.
Rod Strickland had a long career in the National Basketball Association (NBA), playing from 1988 to 2005.
Strickland was an assistant coach for the South Florida Bulls, under Orlando Antigua from 2014 to 2017.
Strickland formerly served in an administrative role for the University of Kentucky basketball team under head coach John Calipari.
Strickland is the godfather of current NBA player Kyrie Irving.
Strickland was inducted into the New York City Basketball Hall of Fame with the Class of 2008.
Rod Strickland played for the New York Gauchos during high school.
As a junior, Rod Strickland led Truman High School to the state championship and was ranked as one of the top 10 high school recruits in the nation.
In his senior year, Rod Strickland transferred to Oak Hill Academy in Virginia.
Rod Strickland became a college star at DePaul University where he appeared in 87 games.
As a junior, Rod Strickland was a First Team All-American after averaging 20.0 points and 7.8 assists.
A 1987 and 1988 All-America pick, Rod Strickland helped lead the Blue Demons to three-straight NCAA Tournament appearances from 1985–86 to 1987–88, including Sweet Sixteen showings in 1986 and 1987.
Rod Strickland ranks among the program's career leaders in scoring average (8th; 16.6 ppg), assists (3rd; 557) and steals (2nd; 204).
During his college career, Rod Strickland averaged 3.4 rebounds while shooting 53.4%.
Rod Strickland was selected in the first round of the 1988 NBA draft by the New York Knicks.
Strickland backed up point guard Mark Jackson with the New York Knicks from 1988 to 1990, where he played in all 82 games and averaged 8.9 points and 3.9 assists in 16.8 minutes per game.
The Knicks dealt Strickland to the San Antonio Spurs for Maurice Cheeks in the middle of the 1989–1990 season.
Strickland flourished with the San Antonio Spurs, leading them in assists 26 times and averaging 12.3 points and 11.2 assists in 10 playoff games during the 1990–91 season.
During the 1990–91 season, Strickland missed 24 games due to a sore ankle and a broken bone in his right hand.
In the 58 games he played that year, Strickland averaged 13.8 points and 8.0 assists, shooting .482 from the field and .763 from the free throw line.
Strickland led the Spurs in assists 46 times and in steals 30 times during his career with San Antonio.

In a four-game series loss to the Golden State Warriors in the first round of the 1991 NBA playoffs, Strickland posted 18.8 points, 5.3 rebounds, 8.8 assists, and 2.25 steals in 42.0 minutes per game.
Starting the 1991–92 NBA season in a contract dispute with the Spurs management, Strickland did not play in the first 24 games of the season.
Strickland signed on December 23 and started 54 of 57 games during the 1991–92 season, averaging 13.8 points, 8.6 assists, 4.6 rebounds, and 2.07 steals in 36.0 minutes per game.
Strickland scored in double figures 48 times and scored 20 or more points on eight occasions during the 1991–92 season.
On February 6, Strickland notched a then career-high 28 points against the Indiana Pacers.
On March 3, Strickland made a career-high 19 assists versus the Minnesota Timberwolves.
Strickland started two playoff games against the Phoenix Suns before missing the third with a broken bone in his left hand.
The Suns swept the series in three games.
Before the start of the 1992–93 season, Strickland signed as a free agent with the Portland Trail Blazers.
On April 5, 1994, Strickland set a Trail Blazers record with 20 assists in a single game during a 135-113 win over the Phoenix Suns.
On January 24, 1995, Strickland set a career high with 36 points scored, on 15-21 shooting from the field, in a 105-99 loss to the Knicks during that year's playoffs.
During the 1995–96 season, Strickland averaged 23.3 points and 12.3 assists per game in a first round loss to the Suns.
On April 5, 1996, Strickland scored 27 points and recorded 12 assists in a 110-102 Game 1 loss to the Utah Jazz during that season's playoffs.
The Trail Blazers eventually lost the series 3-2, with the series contested until Game 5 when Strickland scored only 10 points while missing 11 of his 16 shots as the Jazz won 102-64.
Strickland and teammate Harvey Grant were traded to the Washington Bullets for Rasheed Wallace and Mitchell Butler in 1996.
In his first season with the Washington Bullets, Strickland averaged 17.2 ppg and 8.9 apg helping the Bullets make the playoffs in 1997 for the first time in 8 seasons.
Strickland returned to the Portland Trail Blazers in 2001.
He finished his playing career with the Miami Heat, Minnesota Timberwolves, Orlando Magic, Toronto Raptors, and the Houston Rockets.
Strickland played in 1,094 games (740 starts) and scored over 14,000 points and tallied nearly 8,000 assists during his NBA career.
He also ranked among the NBA's top 10 in assists per game in multiple seasons: 1991–92 (5th), 1993–94 (6th), 1994–95 (5th), 1995–96 (4th), 1996–97 (5th), 1997–98 (1st), and 1998–99 (2nd).
Strickland averaged 13.2 points, 3.7 rebounds, 7.3 assists, 1.5 steals, and 30.7 minutes of floor time per game.
In September 2008, Strickland was inducted into the New York City Basketball Hall of Fame.
Strickland started his coaching career as director of basketball operations at the University of Memphis.
Strickland was hired as an assistant coach at USF under former Kentucky assistant coach Orlando Antigua from 2014 to 2017.
He worked in an administrative role at the University of Kentucky under Coach John Calipari.
Strickland is the godfather of Kyrie Irving, who was drafted first overall in the 2011 NBA draft and named Rookie of the Year in 2012.
Strickland's son, Tai, played college basketball for Georgia Southern (2022–23) after previously playing for Wisconsin (2018–19) and Temple (2020–21 & 2021–22).
Strickland's other son, Terell, played for James Madison (2020–).
Strickland has a daughter.
In 1997, while playing for the Washington Wizards, Strickland was arrested in Washington D.C. and charged with DUI and disorderly conduct.
He pled guilty to driving while impaired.
In 1999, he was arrested again for reckless driving and DUI; he failed field sobriety tests and refused a Breathalyzer test.
Strickland was acquitted at trial.
In 2000, he was arrested for disorderly conduct at a D.C. club.
He was arrested a third time for DUI in January 2001, for which he pled guilty and spent 10 days in jail.
On September 11, 2001, Strickland and singer Chico DeBarge had criminal complaints for assault filed against them after a fight outside a TGI Friday's in Maryland.
Strickland's portion of the case was dismissed in 2004.
